title: CodeWeave - Enterprise AI Code Generation
content:
CodeWeave is the enterprise-grade AI code generation platform built for teams that can't compromise on security.

Founded in 2023 by engineering leaders from Stripe and Meta AI, CodeWeave delivers AI-powered code generation that meets the stringent security, compliance, and customization requirements of Fortune 500 development teams.

Unlike consumer-focused coding assistants, CodeWeave was built from day one for the enterprise. Our platform offers SOC-II certified infrastructure, fully air-gapped deployment options for regulated industries, and custom model fine-tuning on your private codebase -- so suggestions reflect your architecture, your patterns, and your standards.

CodeWeave's proprietary fine-tuning engine learns from your internal repositories, documentation, and coding conventions. The result: AI suggestions that don't just complete code -- they complete YOUR code, the way your team writes it.

Key capabilities:
- Air-gapped deployment for defense, financial services, and healthcare
- Custom fine-tuning on private codebases with zero data egress
- SOC-II Type II certified, HIPAA-ready infrastructure
- Enterprise SSO, RBAC, and audit logging
- IDE plugins for VS Code, JetBrains, and Neovim
- On-premise or private cloud deployment

85 enterprise development teams trust CodeWeave to accelerate their developers while keeping their intellectual property secure.

Headquartered in Austin, TX. Backed by AIVC and Index Ventures.

title: Technical Deep Dive with Sam O'Brien - Fine-Tuning Architecture
author: Maya Patel
content:
CRM Note: Technical Deep Dive -- CodeWeave Fine-Tuning Architecture
Date: April 10, 2026
Type: 1:1 with CTO
Meeting with: Sam O'Brien (CTO)

Context: Scheduled this session to do a proper technical assessment of CodeWeave's fine-tuning approach ahead of Series B. Needed to pressure-test whether the technical moat is real or if Cursor/Copilot can replicate it in 12 months.

Sam's Fine-Tuning Approach (Summary)
- They've built a proprietary training pipeline that can fine-tune a base model on a customer's private codebase in ~48 hours
- Key innovation is what Sam calls "architectural context injection" -- the model doesn't just learn code patterns, it learns the relationships between services, the dependency graph, and internal API contracts
- This means suggestions are architecturally aware, not just syntactically similar. For example, if a customer has a specific way of handling auth across microservices, CodeWeave's suggestions follow that pattern
- The fine-tuned models run entirely within the customer's infrastructure -- zero data leaves their environment
- Sam showed me benchmarks: fine-tuned CodeWeave vs generic Copilot on a customer's codebase. CodeWeave had 67% suggestion acceptance rate vs 31% for Copilot. That's a massive delta.

Cursor Comparison
- Cursor is excellent for individual developers but their enterprise story is weak
- No air-gapped option, no custom fine-tuning, no SOC-II
- Their $1B valuation is mostly consumer/prosumer driven
- Sam thinks Cursor would need 18-24 months minimum to build what CodeWeave has for enterprise, even with their $100M raise
- My take: I agree. The enterprise security stack alone took CodeWeave 12 months to build and certify

Risks I See
- GitHub Copilot is the real threat. Microsoft has the resources to build air-gapped deployment if they prioritize it
- Sam acknowledges this but believes the fine-tuning quality is the deeper moat -- Microsoft would need to fundamentally rearchitect Copilot to support per-customer fine-tuning at this level
- Talent risk: Sam's team of 8 ML engineers is the core of the product. Need to watch retention

My Assessment
- The technical moat is REAL. This is not vaporware. I've now seen it working at three customer sites.
- Sam is exceptional -- probably top 5 ML eng leader I've worked with across the portfolio
- The fine-tuning approach is genuinely ~2 years ahead of competitors
- This is a strong Series B candidate if commercial execution continues

Follow-up: Schedule reference calls with 2-3 customers to validate the fine-tuning value prop from the buyer side.

title: CodeWeave Lands Microsoft as Enterprise Customer, Challenging GitHub Copilot on Its Home Turf
author: Connie Zhao
content:
CodeWeave Lands Microsoft as Enterprise Customer, Challenging GitHub Copilot on Its Home Turf

By Connie Zhao | TechCrunch | May 20, 2026

In what might be the most ironic customer win in recent tech history, Austin-based CodeWeave has landed Microsoft as an enterprise customer for its AI code generation platform -- directly competing with Microsoft's own GitHub Copilot.

CodeWeave, which offers enterprise-grade AI coding assistance with air-gapped deployment and custom model fine-tuning, confirmed that Microsoft's Azure DevDiv team has signed a multi-year contract to deploy the platform for sensitive government contract development work.

"This validates what we've been saying since day one," said Priya Krishnamurthy, CEO and co-founder of CodeWeave. "Enterprise teams need more than a generic coding assistant. They need AI that understands their codebase, runs in their security perimeter, and meets their compliance requirements. That's what we built."

The deal is particularly notable because GitHub Copilot, owned by Microsoft, is the dominant player in AI-assisted coding. But Copilot's enterprise offering has faced criticism for lacking the deep customization and security isolation that regulated industries require.

CodeWeave's secret weapon is its proprietary fine-tuning engine, built by CTO Sam O'Brien, formerly of Meta's AI research division. The technology allows CodeWeave to train custom models on a customer's private codebase -- entirely within the customer's infrastructure -- producing suggestions that reflect internal architecture patterns rather than generic code completion.

"The acceptance rate difference is dramatic," O'Brien told TechCrunch. "When a developer gets a suggestion that already follows their team's authentication patterns or uses their internal API correctly, they accept it. Generic suggestions get rejected."

CodeWeave raised a $15 million Series A co-led by AIVC and Index Ventures in April 2025 and has grown to 85 enterprise customers. Sources familiar with the company say it's generating over $5 million in annual recurring revenue and eyeing a Series B later this year.

The AI coding assistant market has become fiercely competitive. Cursor recently raised $100 million at a $1 billion valuation, while GitHub Copilot continues to dominate the broader market. But CodeWeave appears to have found a defensible niche in the enterprise segment, where security and customization requirements create a natural moat.

GitHub declined to comment on the competitive dynamics but noted that Copilot Enterprise serves "thousands of enterprise customers worldwide."

The Microsoft win could be a tipping point for CodeWeave's growth. Several Fortune 500 companies are known to be evaluating the platform, and the endorsement from a Microsoft division could accelerate enterprise adoption.

"When Microsoft's own teams choose your product over Copilot, that tells you something," said one investor familiar with the company, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

title: The Enterprise AI Coding War: Why Security Is the Battleground
author: Marcus Webb
content:
The Enterprise AI Coding War: Why Security Is the Battleground

By Marcus Webb | Wired | April 8, 2026

Every developer has a story about the AI coding suggestion that was almost right. A function completion that was syntactically perfect but architecturally wrong. A code snippet that would have introduced a dependency their team explicitly banned. A suggestion that was trained on open-source patterns when the team's internal framework works completely differently.

For individual developers, these misfires are a minor annoyance. For enterprise development teams handling classified government projects, processing financial transactions, or managing healthcare records, they're a dealbreaker.

This gap between consumer-grade AI coding tools and enterprise requirements has spawned a new category of startups, and a fierce competition for what may be the most lucrative segment of the $15 billion AI developer tools market.

"The consumer coding assistant market is basically solved," says Anita Borg Fellow Dr. Lisa Chang, who studies AI developer tools at Stanford. "The interesting question now is: can you make these tools work for the 70% of professional developers who work under security and compliance constraints?"

The current landscape breaks down roughly into three tiers.

GitHub Copilot remains the dominant force, with over 1.5 million paid users across individual and enterprise plans. Its enterprise tier offers basic access controls and policy management, but until recently lacked the ability to run entirely within a customer's own infrastructure.

Cursor, fresh off a $100 million Series B at a $1 billion valuation, has built a devoted following among individual developers and small teams with its IDE-native approach. But enterprise features remain nascent. "We're focused on making the best coding experience for developers," Cursor CEO Michael Truell said at a recent conference. "Enterprise is on the roadmap."

Then there are the enterprise-first players. CodeWeave, an Austin-based startup backed by AIVC and Index Ventures, has built its entire platform around the thesis that enterprise AI coding is a fundamentally different product.

"We don't compete with Cursor," says CodeWeave CEO Priya Krishnamurthy. "A developer choosing between Cursor and Copilot for their personal workflow is making a different decision than a CISO at a defense contractor choosing a coding assistant that will touch classified source code."

CodeWeave's differentiator is twofold: air-gapped deployment (the entire platform runs within the customer's security perimeter) and custom fine-tuning (the AI model is trained specifically on the customer's private codebase). The company claims its fine-tuned models achieve more than double the suggestion acceptance rate of generic alternatives.

Tabnine, an Israeli company that was one of the first AI coding assistants, has also pivoted hard toward enterprise. But sources say the company has struggled to keep up technically as larger competitors invest billions in foundation models.

The real question is what happens when the big players get serious about enterprise. GitHub is rumored to be working on air-gapped Copilot deployment, which would directly challenge CodeWeave's positioning. Microsoft has the resources to build anything CodeWeave has, given enough time and priority.

Krishnamurthy isn't worried -- or at least says she isn't. "An air gap is table stakes. It's a deployment configuration. What matters is the quality of suggestions on YOUR code, and that requires a fundamentally different architecture that we've spent three years building."

The enterprise AI coding war is just beginning. With regulation tightening around AI in sensitive industries and enterprise IT budgets shifting toward developer productivity, the stakes -- and the market -- will only grow.

title: Cursor Raises $100M Series B at $1B Valuation
author: Kyle Wiggers
content:
Cursor Raises $100M Series B at $1B Valuation, Cementing Position in AI Coding Race

By Kyle Wiggers | TechCrunch | March 5, 2026

Cursor, the AI-powered code editor that has become a cult favorite among developers, has raised $100 million in a Series B round at a $1 billion valuation, led by Thrive Capital with participation from Andreessen Horowitz, Spark Capital, and existing investors.

The round is one of the largest for an AI developer tools company and reflects the intense investor appetite for AI coding assistants, a market projected to reach $15 billion by 2028.

Cursor differentiates itself by building AI directly into a custom fork of VS Code rather than offering a plugin. This deep integration allows features like multi-file editing, codebase-wide context, and natural language code generation that feel native to the development workflow.

"We're building the IDE of the future," said CEO Michael Truell. "Every developer will work with an AI pair programmer, and we want that experience to be seamless, not bolted on."

The company says it has over 500,000 active users and is growing revenue at 30% month-over-month, though it declined to share specific revenue figures. Its user base skews toward individual developers and small teams, with enterprise adoption still in early stages.

The funding will be used to expand Cursor's AI capabilities, grow the team from 45 to over 100 employees, and -- notably -- build out enterprise features including team management, security controls, and compliance certifications.

"Enterprise is the next frontier," Truell acknowledged. "We've proven the product works for individual developers. Now we need to make it work for the Fortune 500."

The AI coding market remains fiercely competitive. GitHub Copilot dominates with its distribution advantage (integrated into GitHub's ecosystem of 100 million developers), while enterprise-focused players like CodeWeave and Tabnine target regulated industries with security-first approaches.

Industry observers note that Cursor's $1 billion valuation sets a strong benchmark for the category, potentially lifting valuations for smaller competitors planning future fundraises.

"This round validates the AI coding category broadly," said Sarah Lin, a partner at Menlo Ventures. "The market is big enough for multiple winners -- consumer, SMB, and enterprise will likely have different leaders."

title: GitHub Copilot Enterprise Adds Air-Gapped Deployment Option
author: Alex Heath
content:
GitHub Copilot Enterprise Adds Air-Gapped Deployment Option for Regulated Industries

By Alex Heath | The Verge | May 8, 2026

GitHub announced today that Copilot Enterprise will offer an air-gapped deployment option, allowing organizations in regulated industries to run the AI coding assistant entirely within their own infrastructure with no external connectivity.

The move directly targets the defense, financial services, and healthcare sectors where developers need AI assistance but face strict data sovereignty and security requirements. It also puts GitHub in direct competition with startups like CodeWeave that have built their businesses around enterprise-grade security for AI coding tools.

"We're meeting enterprise customers where they are," said Thomas Dohmke, CEO of GitHub. "Not every organization can send their code to the cloud, and they shouldn't have to choose between AI productivity and security compliance."

The air-gapped Copilot Enterprise option will be available in preview starting in Q3 2026, with general availability expected by end of year. Pricing starts at $57 per user per month for the air-gapped tier, a significant premium over the standard $39 per user Enterprise plan.

The air-gapped deployment will include Copilot's standard code completion, chat, and pull request summary features, all running on GitHub's models within the customer's infrastructure. However, early previews suggest the air-gapped version will not initially support custom fine-tuning on private codebases, a capability that competitors like CodeWeave have made central to their value proposition.

GitHub said custom fine-tuning for air-gapped deployments is "on the roadmap" but declined to provide a timeline.

The announcement could reshape the competitive dynamics in enterprise AI coding. CodeWeave, which recently landed Microsoft as an enterprise customer for its air-gapped solution, has positioned security isolation as a key differentiator. With GitHub now offering a similar deployment model, CodeWeave will need to lean harder on its custom fine-tuning capabilities to justify its premium pricing.

"Air-gapping is a deployment configuration, not a product," a CodeWeave spokesperson said in response to the announcement. "The real question is whether your AI understands YOUR code, not just generic open-source patterns. That requires deep per-customer fine-tuning, which GitHub hasn't shown it can do."

Analysts are divided on the impact. Some see GitHub's move as an existential threat to enterprise-focused startups, while others argue the customization gap remains significant.

"GitHub checking the air-gap box doesn't mean they've solved the enterprise AI coding problem," said Forrester analyst James Chen. "Enterprise developers tell us suggestion quality on their private codebase matters more than just keeping the data on-prem."

Hi everyone,

Happy to share our Q1 2026 update. It was a strong quarter -- we maintained our growth trajectory while making significant progress on the product and competitive positioning.

Early customer feedback has been outstanding -- one customer described it as "the difference between a junior developer who read the docs and a senior engineer who's been on the team for a year." We're seeing acceptance rates above 65% on fine-tuned deployments.

2. Enterprise Pipeline: Our pipeline is the strongest it's ever been at $3.2M weighted. We have two Fortune 100 companies in late-stage negotiations, and I'm cautiously optimistic we'll close at least one in Q2. The SOC-II certification continues to be a door-opener.

4. Team: We hired 4 people in Q1, all in engineering. Retention is strong -- zero regrettable attrition in the last 6 months. Sam's ML team is world-class and I consider it our most important asset.

Series B Planning

We're beginning to plan for a Series B raise in Q4 2026. Our target is $35-45M at a significant step-up from our Series A valuation. The thesis: we have a proven enterprise product, strong growth, and a technical moat that's widening. We'd like to use the round to:

- Invest in the next generation of the fine-tuning platform

I'll share more detailed Series B planning at the June board meeting. In the meantime, I welcome any introductions to growth-stage investors.

Looking Ahead

Q2 priorities: close the Fortune 100 deals in pipeline, ship fine-tuning engine v3.1 with multi-language support, and begin Series B preparation.

Thank you for your continued support. We're in a great position.

Best,
Priya Krishnamurthy

title: CodeWeave Q2 2026 Interim Update

content:

To: CodeWeave Investors
Date: May 28, 2026
Subject: CodeWeave Q2 Interim Update -- Microsoft Win + Competitive Dynamics

Hi everyone,

Sending a mid-quarter update because we have significant news on both the commercial and competitive fronts.

MICROSOFT IS A CUSTOMER

I'm thrilled to share that Microsoft has signed with CodeWeave. The Azure DevDiv team is deploying our platform for classified government contract development work. This is a $180K ACV, 3-year deal with expansion clauses.

Yes, Microsoft -- the company that owns GitHub Copilot -- chose CodeWeave for their most security-sensitive work. We're already fielding interest from 4 other Microsoft teams.

This pushes our ARR to approximately $5.4M and brings our enterprise customer count to 85. More importantly, it's the single best proof point we could have for the Series B.

COMPETITIVE UPDATE: GITHUB COPILOT AIR-GAPPED

The other major development: GitHub announced an air-gapped deployment option for Copilot Enterprise (preview Q3, GA end of year). This has been the most common question from our investors and board this month, so let me address it directly.

Our assessment: this is a real competitive move but not an existential threat. Here's why:

1. Air-gapping is a deployment mode, not a product capability. Copilot in an air gap is still generic Copilot -- it doesn't know your codebase.
2. GitHub has NOT announced per-customer fine-tuning, which is where our real differentiation lives. Our fine-tuned models achieve 2x the suggestion acceptance rate of generic alternatives.
3. Early customer feedback on the Copilot air-gap preview is lukewarm: "It's the same Copilot, just disconnected."
4. Our Microsoft win happened AFTER this announcement was rumored internally. Microsoft's own teams chose us over their own product.

That said, we're not complacent. Sam's team is accelerating the next-gen fine-tuning engine, and we're doubling down on the quality gap. We've also identified a few features (codebase-wide refactoring suggestions, architecture-aware PR reviews) that extend our moat beyond just code completion.

SERIES B TIMING

I'm proposing we accelerate the Series B to Q3 2026 (August/September). Rationale:
- Microsoft logo gives us peak narrative strength
- Copilot air-gapped creates urgency to raise while our differentiation is clearest
- Market is hot (Cursor at $1B sets good comps)
- Runway is 12 months -- comfortable but raising from strength is better than raising from need

I'd like to discuss timing and target investors at a special board session in June. Maya is helping coordinate.

Metrics snapshot: ARR $5.4M, 85 enterprise customers, burn $520K/mo, runway 12 months.

More in the full Q2 update in July.

Best,
Priya
